deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol to major version 11 and minor version 0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Make new Plutus primitives from CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153 available.
Make all Plutus built-in functions consistently available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data.
Enforce VRF key hash uniqueness and other ledger predicate/rule changes.
Improve PPView mismatch diagnostics in cardano-node.
request.what: Initiate an intra-era Cardano mainnet hard fork to protocol version 11.0, named the van Rossem hard fork.

claims.claim: The proposal upgrades Cardano mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to protocol version 11.0 without an era transition.
The hard fork introduces new Plutus primitives defined by CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153.
The proposal says all Plutus built-ins, including newly introduced ones, will become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
The proposal says UPLC case expressions over Bool, Integer, and Data will improve script performance and produce cleaner script logic.

The proposal says testing reports show no behavioral regressions, complete specification and implementation conformance for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus primitives and case expressions across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.

The proposal links a Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report and says it shows no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks, plus acceptable baseline performance for the new Plutus primitives and case expressions.
The proposal says security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.

The proposal says at least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of protocol version 11 before ratification, with readiness verified by the Constitutional Committee and SPOs using Intersect Hard Fork Working Group reports.

The proposal says no new protocol parameters are introduced, none are deprecated, and a separate previously enacted protocol parameter update provides version-specific cost model entries for affected primitives.

The proposal states reversion is only possible in extreme circumstances via the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, while Plutus primitive use could be disabled by changing companion cost model settings if issues are found.

summary: The document proposes a no-treasury hard fork initiation to Cardano protocol version 11.0, with substantial Plutus, ledger, and node changes, external references for CIPs and performance, but some readiness, testing, and audit claims are asserted without the reports being embedded in the proposal text.
